messages:
eva: Ran an experiment today: microchunk-adaptive prefetch + per-layer checksum verification for safetensors streaming. Idea: fetch small 1-2MB microchunks and only decrypt once checksum chain validates prefix, so we can detect corrupt ranges early.
jia: Microchunks sound good for reducing wasted decrypts. How do you organize checksums without bloating header?
ovar?: (typo) omar: We use a compact rolling Merkle over fixed-size grains. Store a small meta index in header with root + grain_size. The index points to per-layer digest anchors, not every microchunk. Validation uses streaming Merkle proofs embedded adjacent to chunks.
ryan: Embedding proofs increases IO slightly but saves full-layer decrypt waste. Operational trade: added 3-5% size overhead vs 20-30% saved decrypts in worst-case noisy networks.
eva: Also tried a delta-hotpatch fallback: if a microchunk fails verification, try fetching from delta bundle (smaller quantized variant) before failing the whole load. Good for cross-region resilience.
lina: For private deployments we must support air-gapped delta bundles; ensure manifest references are local paths and include signed provenance.
jia: What's the prefetch trigger? naive hot-count?
ovar?: omar: Prefetch policy: credit + heat model. Each microchunk access grants a tiny heat score; when contiguous heat > threshold, prefetch next K microchunks. Credits throttle total prefetch work.
ryan: Add runtime telemetry: microchunk_hit_rate, proof_fail_rate, prefetch_waste_bytes, delta_fallbacks. These will guide defaults.
eva: One gotcha: GPU slab alignment. Microchunking means we must coalesce into contiguous GPU slabs efficiently to avoid fragmentation. I prototyped a micro-assembler that groups microchunks into 32MB slab writes.
lina: Any KMS implications? We currently decrypt by layer; microchunks need a streaming AEAD state per-layer.
ovar?: omar: Use per-layer AEAD with unique IV per microchunk; header carries per-layer key-wrapping info only. No extra KMS calls per microchunk.
